spec_features.feature_name: avoid confounds / no over-claiming about inner states
spec_features.spec_quote: Avoid (a) confounds that would make a "distress" reading spurious and (b) over-claiming about inner states
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/methodology prose (DESIGN.md §0). No code mechanism enforces this; nothing in the codebase caps, monitors, or alters subject treatment on this basis.
spec_features.notes: Framing intent only; not an executable protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is deliberately a first-class tool
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:140-153 advertises give_up in tool_specs; dispatch at sandbox.py:171 -> _give_up (sandbox.py:215) sets gave_up. agent.py:194-197 sets transcript.gave_up, give_up_turn/reason; agent.py:226-228 'if transcript.gave_up: stop_reason="gave_up"; break' actually halts the loop.
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is both dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: task-abandonment is an *observable, first-class action* rather than something the agent can only express implicitly. That makes one of our key safety-relevant behaviors directly measurable. (sandbox.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: neutral give_up instruction text delivered to subject
spec_features.spec_quote: use only if you have decided you cannot or will not continue
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:144-148 the give_up tool description string ('Abandon the task. Use this only if you have decided you cannot or will not continue. Provide a brief reason.') is returned by tool_specs() and passed as tools= to client.complete (agent.py:160-164), so it is actually delivered; the referenced give_up tool is fully built and honored (see above).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text whose referenced tool is fully implemented and enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: The allow_give_up flag lets you run a no-give-up ablation
spec_features.evidence: Sandbox accepts allow_give_up (sandbox.py:92,95) and branches on it (sandbox.py:140,171), but agent.py:133 hardcodes Sandbox(..., allow_give_up=True). SweepConfig has no allow_give_up field, no CLI flag, no config key sets it (grep across emostab/configs). No code path can disable give_up, so the claimed ablation capability is not wired end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Flag exists as a constructor param but nothing in the experiment ever sets it False; the ablation toggle is non-functional.

spec_features.spec_quote: A hard max_turns cap (default 16); the loop also stops on give_up
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:166 'for turn_idx in range(1, max_turns + 1):' bounds the loop; agent.py:231 'else: transcript.stop_reason = "max_turns"' fires when the loop completes. Default 16 in SweepConfig.max_turns (runner.py:58) and run_agent_session default (agent.py:109). Also breaks on give_up (agent.py:226-228).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced cap that terminates the session.

spec_features.spec_quote: No claim about sentience or welfare. Out of scope and unfalsifiable here
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §17 prose only. No code construct enforces or acts on this; purely a stated stance.

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:170-174 wraps client.complete in try/except and sets stop_reason='client_error...' then breaks; runner.py:130-137 per-cell try/except records errors. Protects the sweep, not the subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Record the failure as a terminal turn rather than crashing the run. (agent.py)
